name: Canada
tagline: Transparent entry requirements, high fees, and a study permit queue
summary: Canada is the most European-feeling option outside Europe: you apply to a named programme, entry requirements are published as IB point thresholds rather than guessed at, and admission is far more predictable than in the United States. Education is run by the provinces, so Ontario has one central application system, British Columbia has another, and Quebec universities take you directly. The two catches are money - international undergraduate tuition typically runs 40,000-70,000 CAD a year - and immigration, because since 2024 Canada has capped the number of study permit applications it will even look at, and undergraduates need a Provincial Attestation Letter to get into that queue.
whyConsider: Entry requirements are published. Universities state the IB points and HL subjects a programme needs, so you can tell in advance whether your predicted score is in range.
Four-year bachelor's degrees with a co-op option at several universities, meaning paid work terms built into the degree - Waterloo built its reputation on this.
A degree from a Canadian university normally leads to a Post-Graduation Work Permit with no field-of-study restriction for bachelor's graduates, which is a clearer route than US OPT.
Both English and French are official languages, and Montreal in particular lets you study in English while living in French.
Class sizes and tuition sit between the European and American extremes, and campuses are safe and well-resourced.
watchOuts: The study permit cap. For 2026 Canada set a ceiling of 309,670 study permit application spaces requiring a Provincial Attestation Letter, split by province. Once a province runs out of attestation letters it stops issuing them for the year, so applying early matters more than it should.
Proof of funds. From 1 September 2026 a single applicant must show 23,448 CAD in living costs on top of first-year tuition and travel money. That is money that must visibly exist, not a promise.
Tuition is not capped for internationals and can rise each year. UBC is unusual in guaranteeing increases of no more than 3% a year for four years after you start.
Ontario's central system has no deadline for international applicants - each university sets its own, which sounds relaxed and is actually a trap.
Winters in Montreal, Toronto, Edmonton and Calgary are far harder than a Danish winter. Vancouver and Victoria are mild but very wet.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No national minimum. Universities set their own; a typical competitive threshold for a good research university is in the high 20s to low 30s, with selective programmes such as engineering, commerce and life sciences asking for more. Exact figures were not verified programme by programme for this guide - read each university's IB requirements page.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Canadian universities normally require the full IB Diploma and then name specific Higher Level subjects for the programme - HL Mathematics for engineering, HL Chemistry and Biology for life sciences, and so on. Standard Level subjects usually satisfy prerequisites only where the university says so explicitly.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: There is no single national conversion. Each university maps IB grades onto its own admission average, and Ontario universities also convert IB grades into percentage equivalents for comparison with Ontario's 4U courses.
notes: Transfer credit for HL subjects graded 5 or above is common and can shorten your degree - ask the specific faculty, not general admissions.
Offers are conditional on your final July 2027 results, so a drop below the conditions can cost you the place.

Quebec is different: its universities run a one-year shorter bachelor's for students who completed CEGEP, but international students with a full IB Diploma are normally admitted to the standard programme length. Confirm the programme length with the university before you accept.

deadlines.label: Check the IB mathematics rule against your subject choices
deadlines.notes: Not a date anyone publishes, and the earliest thing here that cannot be repaired later. Toronto accepts Mathematics: Applications and Interpretations SL for the Advanced Functions prerequisite only; UBC excludes it from its science programmes, the Faculty of Management, Sauder and the Vancouver School of Economics; McGill will not take it as a mathematics prerequisite at all. Dalhousie will. The choice is made in the first weeks of DP1, two years before any deadline on this page, and no Canadian university has an appeal route for it.

deadlines.label: Ontario — OUAC application, international and out-of-province applicants (Group B)
deadlines.audience: international and out-of-province applicants (OUAC Group B)
deadlines.notes: The OUAC's wording is exact and it is the whole of the answer: "There is no specific Undergraduate application deadline if you are a Group B applicant. Deadlines vary at each university and sometimes depend on the program." It adds the warning that costs people places: "You must ensure the OUAC has enough time to process your choices before the universities' program deadlines" — so the university's date is not the date you can submit on. Do not take the OUAC's own headline dates for yours. 15 January 2027 and 28 May 2027 are published on the same page under Group A, which is an applicant currently taking Ontario high school courses and under 21 — not a Danish IB candidate. The University of Toronto's own dates are recorded as separate entries below; the other five Ontario universities in this record were not established and no date has been invented for them. How this page was read: ouac.on.ca returns HTTP 403 to every automated fetch, so it was opened in a browser on 23 September 2026, where the page carries its own "Last updated: September 14, 2026". Its dates are inside collapsed accordions and are absent from the page text until each is clicked, so a scraped copy of this page shows no dates at all even if it gets past the 403.

deadlines.label: Ontario — University of Toronto, recommended early application date
deadlines.notes: Toronto's 2027 admissions table gives this under the heading "Recommended early application date" for Applied Science & Engineering, Architecture, Arts & Science at St George, the iSchool, Kinesiology & Physical Education, Mississauga and Scarborough. Applying by this date and getting your documents in by 1 December 2026 — its own entry below — buys early consideration, which is an earlier decision rather than a better one. Music runs its own recommended date of 1 December, and Medical Radiation Sciences has none. Missing it costs you nothing except the earlier answer; the date that closes the door is 15 January 2027.

deadlines.label: Ontario — University of Toronto, documents for early consideration
deadlines.audience: applicants who applied by the 7 November early date
deadlines.notes: Early consideration is conditional on both halves: the application by 7 November 2026 and the required documents by this date. Applying early and sending the documents in January puts you back in the ordinary queue. Your gymnasium supplies most of what is wanted, so ask for it in October rather than in the last week of November. Promoted out of the Toronto early-application note so that it can be sorted, counted and shown on a calendar.

deadlines.label: Ontario — University of Toronto applications close
deadlines.notes: Published on Toronto's 2027 admissions deadlines table under "Deadline" for Applied Science & Engineering, Architecture, Arts & Science at St George including the International Foundation Program, the iSchool, Kinesiology & Physical Education, Music, Nursing, Physician Assistant, Mississauga and Scarborough. Medical Radiation Sciences is the exception at 1 February. This is the university's own date, not the OUAC's, and you apply through the OUAC — which warns that it needs processing time before a university's date, so treat the first week of January as the real one. Promoted out of the OUAC Group B note above, where it was the only Ontario date on the record and was not sortable.

deadlines.label: Ontario — University of Toronto, supporting documents
deadlines.notes: Two weeks after the application itself, and invisible to a student who thinks submitting the application ended the job. Music is the exception and wants its documents on 15 January with the application. An application whose documents never arrive is not assessed.

deadlines.label: Ontario — accept the offer and pay the deposit
deadlines.notes: Set in each university's own offer letter, and there is no Ontario-wide date for you. The OUAC publishes 1 June 2027 as "the earliest date a Group A applicant may be required to respond to an Ontario university offer of admission and give a financial commitment" — registration deposit, residence deposit, the lot. Read the words: it protects Group A applicants specifically, an applicant currently in an Ontario high school and under 21. It is not a promise to you, and an Ontario university may lawfully ask a Group B applicant for money before June. Ask the university what your response date is at the moment the offer arrives; do not count to 1 June.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — create and confirm an EducationPlannerBC account
deadlines.notes: Nothing can be submitted until the confirmation email has been acted on, so this is a task to finish in the week the applications open rather than the week they close. Use a personal address rather than a school one: the platform warns that school accounts are deactivated at graduation and the institutions correspond with the address on the account long afterwards.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — UBC applications open
deadlines.notes: UBC publishes this as "Early October 2026" — a month without a day — for the Winter Session running September 2027 to April 2028. There is no date here to count down to because UBC has not published one. Simon Fraser, on the same EducationPlannerBC platform, does give a day: 1 October 2026. Checking UBC's page in the last week of September 2026 is the only way to catch the opening.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — UBC, the date for international applicants and for the International Scholars Program awards
deadlines.audience: international applicants, and anyone seeking a UBC International Scholars Program award
deadlines.notes: Two months before UBC's general January deadline, and the single most missable date in British Columbia for a Danish applicant: it is the date by which an international student must have applied to UBC and submitted the award application to be considered for the International Scholars Program. The scholarship is the reason the date exists, and the scholarship is the thing that is gone on 16 November — the general admission route stays open until 15 January. Published with a time and a time zone, 11:59 p.m. PST, which is 08:59 the following morning in Denmark; a Danish applicant working to a local midnight has until the morning of 16 November, but do not use that margin.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — Simon Fraser University, Undergraduate Scholars Entrance Scholarship closes
deadlines.audience: applicants seeking an SFU entrance scholarship
deadlines.notes: Six weeks before Simon Fraser's own application deadline, which is the trap: a student who applies in January, on time, has already missed the entrance scholarship by a month. The supporting documents for the scholarship are due separately on 31 January 2027, and the offers go out between mid-March and May. Read in a browser on 23 September 2026 from SFU's Fall 2027 dates page, because sfu.ca closes the socket on every automated fetch.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — UBC applications close
deadlines.notes: Published as "Deadline to apply for Winter Session (September 2027 to April 2028)", 11:59 p.m. PST. Submitted through EducationPlannerBC, not to UBC directly. Promoted out of the University of Victoria note below, where it sat as a comparison rather than as a date of its own.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — Simon Fraser University applications close
deadlines.notes: Published as "Deadline to apply for Fall 2027 on Education Planner BC", with applications opening 1 October 2026. Two weeks later than UBC, on the same platform, in the same city region — which is the argument against carrying one British Columbian date to another. Promoted out of the University of Victoria note below.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — UBC, documents and the English Language Admission Standard
deadlines.notes: UBC gives international applicants sixteen days after the application to meet the English Language Admission Standard for direct entry and to submit the documents required for admission. An IB Diploma taught in English usually satisfies the standard, but UBC states the requirement without an automatic IB exemption, so establish in writing which of the standard's routes yours is before January rather than after it. A separate 15 February 2027 date exists for submitting evidence that the standard is met.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — Simon Fraser University, Beedie and Contemporary Arts supplemental requirements
deadlines.audience: applicants to the Beedie School of Business or the School for the Contemporary Arts
deadlines.notes: Beedie applicants must complete every item on their To-Do List by this date; School for the Contemporary Arts applicants — excluding Art, Performance and Cinema Studies and Performance Production & Design — must complete an audition, interview or portfolio by it. A portfolio or audition is weeks of work, not an afternoon, and the date is published nowhere a student sees before applying.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — Simon Fraser University, admission documents
deadlines.notes: Published as the "Admission document submission deadline for all High School Applicants", four weeks after the application. Admission decisions are made on a rolling basis from January to late April, so documents that arrive in February are read against whatever places are left rather than against the whole field.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — University of Victoria applications close
deadlines.notes: UVic publishes its deadlines on each programme page rather than centrally, and says so, so there is no single Victoria date to record and none has been invented. UBC's 15 January 2027 and Simon Fraser's 31 January 2027 are each recorded above as their own entries; do not assume UVic matches either, and read the date off the programme page you are actually applying to.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — Simon Fraser University, accept your offer
deadlines.notes: Published as "Accept your offer — Deadline for most students to accept their offer of admission", and it is also the residence and housing application deadline, so a student who accepts on the last day is applying for a room on the last day too. "Most students" is SFU's own hedge; your offer letter governs. Note how far this is from Ontario's shape: the OUAC's 1 June protection does not exist in British Columbia, and 1 May here is a real date a month earlier.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — UBC, final official transcript, and the IB timing problem nobody resolves
deadlines.notes: Published as "Deadline to have your final official transcript mailed to UBC". For an IB candidate the two dates do not fit: IB results are released on about 6 July 2027, six days after this deadline. UBC's own IB page does not resolve it — it says only that "Initial admission decisions are based on interim grades as reported by your high school. Once your final IB results are available, we will use them to confirm your admission decision", and that to be assessed for first-year credit you must "contact the IBO and have your official results submitted to UBC electronically". Both pages were read on 23 September 2026 and neither states an IB-specific deadline or an exception to 30 June. This is a gap in UBC's publishing rather than a contradiction between two UBC statements, and it has not been resolved in either direction here. What to do: request the electronic transmission from the IB in the spring, so that it fires the day results are released, and ask UBC admissions in writing which date applies to an IB candidate before you rely on either.

deadlines.label: British Columbia — enrol in the Medical Services Plan on arrival
deadlines.notes: Compulsory for a study permit of six months or more, and cover begins only after the balance of the arrival month plus two more. Arrive in late August for a September start and you are outside the provincial plan until 1 November, so carry private insurance until then.

deadlines.label: Apply direct — build the list of dates yourself, one university at a time
deadlines.notes: The defining property of the direct route, which serves Quebec, Alberta and Nova Scotia. No portal, no shared account, no shared calendar, and no page anywhere that lists your universities together. McGill's and Concordia's dates are recorded as their own entries below and they are six weeks apart for two universities two miles apart in the same city; Alberta publishes per programme and Dalhousie had not published 2027 at all when this was checked. Build the list yourself in the autumn of DP2 and put every date in your own calendar, because nothing will remind you.

deadlines.label: Quebec — McGill University applications close
deadlines.audience: applicants studying at, or last studied at, an overseas or US high school
deadlines.notes: McGill states it with the year and the weekday attached — "Friday, January 15, 2027" — as the "Application deadline for Fall 2027 admission to undergraduate programs by applicants studying or who last studied in an overseas or U.S. high school", which is the group a Danish IB candidate is in. No closing time is published on that page. McGill assesses on predicted IB results or, if you have them, on final ones. Promoted out of the apply-direct note above so that it can be sorted, counted and shown on a calendar.

deadlines.label: Quebec — Concordia University, US and international applicants
deadlines.notes: Concordia's wording is "U.S. and international applicants: Apply no later than February 1 to allow time for immigration document processing" — a month before its own general deadline, and the reason is the Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec, which has its own entry below and has to be granted before the federal study permit. Published as a bare "February 1" with no calendar year, as every date in that section is, so the year here is read into the autumn 2027 intake this profile covers and the entry is marked provisional. This is the Concordia date that belongs to a Danish applicant; 1 March is not yours.

deadlines.label: Quebec — Concordia University, fall entry, general deadline
deadlines.audience: applicants who are not applying from outside Canada
deadlines.notes: Published as "FALL ENTRY (September) Deadline: March 1", a bare day with no calendar year, so the year here is read into the intake this profile covers and the entry is marked provisional. Recorded because it is the date a Danish student will see first on Concordia's page and it is the wrong one for them: the international date is 1 February, four weeks earlier, and it is the entry above.

deadlines.label: Alberta — University of Alberta and University of Calgary applications close
deadlines.notes: Alberta publishes its Fall 2027 deadlines per programme behind a faculty-and-term filter rather than as one institutional date, so there is no single date to record and none has been invented. The page states that its deadlines "are valid for applications to the Fall 2027, Winter 2028, Spring 2028 and Summer 2028 terms", so the 2027 dates do exist — they are simply not reachable without choosing a programme first. Read yours off the programme. The minimum admission average also varies by faculty and changes every year, so last year's cut-off is not a target.

deadlines.label: Nova Scotia — Dalhousie University applications close
deadlines.notes: In September 2026 Dalhousie was still publishing September 2026 entry dates and nothing for 2027. Its shape is known and is recorded here as precedent rather than as a prediction: for September 2026 entry the competitive health programmes — Nursing, Health Sciences, Medical Sciences and Social Work — closed on 15 February 2026, and applications to everything else were considered up to the start of classes where space remained. If 2027 follows 2026, mid-February is the date that matters and everything after it is a lottery on leftover places. Recheck from about November 2026.

deadlines.label: Quebec — apply for the Certificat d'acceptation du Quebec
deadlines.notes: A Quebec immigration document with its own fee and its own financial test, required in addition to the federal study permit and granted before it. There is no published deadline because it is gated on your offer, not on a date — which is why it is the largest practical difference between choosing Montreal and choosing Toronto, and why Concordia asks international applicants to apply on 1 February rather than 1 March. Start it the day the offer arrives.

deadlines.label: Provincial Attestation Letter — outside Quebec
deadlines.notes: Requested by the university after you accept its offer, so there is no date you act on — but there is a quantity, and the quantity is the risk. In 2026 the allocations were Ontario 104,780, Quebec 93,069, British Columbia 32,596, Alberta 32,271 and Nova Scotia 8,480, out of 309,670 nationally: the maximum number of study permit applications Canada would accept for processing in the year. Master's and doctoral students at public institutions stopped needing a letter on 1 January 2026; a bachelor's student did not. No 2027 allocation had been published as of 23 September 2026, and the 2026 figures above are recorded as precedent, not as next year's ceiling.

deadlines.label: Study permit application
deadlines.notes: As soon as you hold the offer and the attestation letter or CAQ — there is no published date and waiting for one is the mistake. A single applicant outside Quebec applying on or after 1 September 2026 must show CAD 23,448 for a year of living expenses, which excludes tuition and travel; the figure is updated each year, so check it rather than budgeting from this one. Quebec sets its own figure through its immigration ministry and it is not the federal one.

steps: Choose the province before you choose the university, because in Canada the province decides how you apply. Ontario goes through the OUAC, British Columbia through EducationPlannerBC, and Quebec, Alberta and Nova Scotia direct to each university. The three routes have different deadlines, different fees and different numbers of choices.

Check the mathematics rule against your IB subject choices, in DP1 rather than in your final year. Toronto, UBC and McGill each refuse Mathematics: Applications and Interpretations SL for their science and business programmes; Dalhousie accepts it. Nothing later can repair that choice.

Read the published IB requirement for each programme you want, on the university’s own page. There is no national rule and the universities genuinely disagree — UBC admits at 24 points including bonus points, Dalhousie at 26 including bonus points, and Toronto reads your total out of 42 with bonus points excluded.

Create the right application account. In Ontario the OUAC charges CAD 159 for three choices and you also pay a document evaluation fee to every separate university. In British Columbia the platform charges nothing and the institution charges its own fee. Applying direct means an account, a fee and a deadline at each university.

Send predicted IB grades and your school transcript. Every route in this Destination decides on predicted results and confirms on final ones, so the offer arrives months before July and is conditional on it.

Accept an offer, pay the deposit, and ask the university to request a Provincial Attestation Letter for you — or, in Quebec, apply for a Certificat d’acceptation du Québec, which is a separate provincial immigration document with its own fee and its own financial test.
Apply for the study permit with the attestation letter or CAQ, your letter of acceptance, proof of CAD 23,448 in living funds outside Quebec plus tuition and travel, and biometrics.

Sort out health cover, which depends on the province and is a separate decision from everything above. Ontario leaves international students outside the public plan for the whole degree; British Columbia, Alberta and Nova Scotia let them in, each on its own terms and each after a wait.
Arrange housing early. Most universities guarantee first-year residence only to students who apply by a separate housing deadline — UBC’s is 1 May 2027.
application.selectionNotes: Admission is mostly grade-based against published thresholds, with supplementary applications, essays or video interviews for a minority of programmes such as Waterloo engineering, Queen's commerce, McMaster health sciences and UBC's broader personal profile. There is no interview for most degrees and no national ranking. You apply to a specific programme and faculty, and switching faculties later is not automatic.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: The entire English-speaking system - every province except Quebec teaches primarily in English, and Quebec has three large English-language universities (McGill, Concordia, Bishop's).
language.englishProof: Universities generally waive English testing for students educated in English, and an IB Diploma with English A is normally accepted as proof. The exact waiver rule differs by university and was not verified individually; where a test is required, typical minimums are IELTS 6.5-7.0 or TOEFL iBT 90-100.
notes: In Quebec you can study entirely in English, but daily life, part-time jobs and paperwork are in French. Quebec has its own immigration rules and its own financial requirement for study permits.
French is useful but never required outside Quebec.

tuitionEuEea.value: Not applicable - Canada has no EU/EEA fee category. Danish students pay international fees.

tuitionNonEu.value: Set by each university and not comparable across provinces. Verified for 2026/27 at UBC: Arts CAD 51,530.40 for a 30-credit year, Science and Computer Science CAD 53,082.00, Engineering CAD 66,199.66 for a 37-credit first year, Commerce (Sauder) CAD 66,678.30. UBC also caps the annual increase at 3% for four years for a student starting in 2026/27. No figure is recorded for Ontario: the University of Toronto states that its fees for an academic year are finalised in the spring of that year, so the price for 2027/28 does not exist yet.

costs.applicationFee: Three different answers, one per route. Ontario: CAD 159 through the OUAC for three programme choices, CAD 51 for each further choice, plus a document evaluation fee to each separate university — CAD 98 at Toronto, CAD 125 at Western, CAD 95 at Queen’s, Waterloo and McMaster, CAD 93 at Ottawa. British Columbia: nothing to the platform, and the institution’s own fee — CAD 130 at Simon Fraser for an international applicant, CAD 184.00 at Victoria where any transcript comes from outside Canada. Direct: one fee per university, CAD 150 at the University of Alberta for a new applicant.

livingCostMonthly.value: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada requires a single study permit applicant outside Quebec to show 23,448 CAD for 12 months of living expenses for applications submitted on or after 1 September 2026 - about 1,954 CAD a month. That is the immigration minimum, not a realistic Vancouver or Toronto budget.

notes: The CAD 23,448 figure covers living expenses only. You must separately show first-year tuition and return travel.
Quebec sets its own financial requirement through its immigration ministry, assessed for the CAQ rather than by IRCC, and it is a different number.

Compulsory student and health fees are charged on top of tuition at every university. In Ontario that includes UHIP, which is mandatory for international students because the provincial plan does not cover them.
Not established: tuition at any Ontario university for 2027/28. Toronto says the figures are set in the spring of the year of entry and publishes no current international rate on its fees page.

funding: Entrance scholarships from the university itself. Most Canadian universities award automatic or competitive entrance awards to strong international applicants; amounts of 5,000-20,000 CAD a year are common and a small number are full-cost. These are usually awarded from your admission application with no separate form, but some require an application by a deadline earlier than the admission deadline.

Named large awards: the University of Toronto's Lester B. Pearson International Scholarships and UBC's International Scholars programmes are the two best known full-cost awards for internationals. Both require nomination by your school, with autumn deadlines well before the admission deadline - ask your studievejleder in September 2026.
Faculty and programme awards, especially in engineering and commerce, awarded after first year on results.
Danish SU may in some circumstances support a full degree abroad. Rules were not verified for this guide - check su.dk and talk to your studievejleder early.
There is no Canadian government grant or loan for international undergraduates. Budget on the assumption you will pay tuition from family funds, savings and scholarships.
workRights: Study permit holders may work while studying and after graduating under conditions set on the permit. After your degree, the Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) is the main route: you must apply within 180 days of confirmation that you completed your studies, your study permit must have been valid during that window, and for a bachelor's, master's or doctoral degree there is no field-of-study restriction - the restriction to shortage occupations applies only to non-degree programmes. Degree graduates must show language ability at CLB 7 in English or NCLC 7 in French across all four skills. Source: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html
residency: You need a study permit, not a visa-free stay. Since 2024 Canada caps the number of study permit applications it will process: for 2026 the cap is 309,670 application spaces for people who need a Provincial or Territorial Attestation Letter, allocated by province (Ontario 104,780, Quebec 93,069, British Columbia 32,596, down to 1,376 in Prince Edward Island). Undergraduates do need a PAL; from 1 January 2026 master's and doctoral students at public institutions do not. Your university requests the PAL for you. No allocation beyond 2026 had been published as of September 2026, so treat the 2027 rules as likely-but-unconfirmed and apply as early as you can. Sources: https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/2026-provincial-territorial-allocations-under-international-student-cap.html
housing: Most universities guarantee residence to first-year students who apply by a separate housing deadline, usually in spring. Take the guarantee - Vancouver and Toronto private rentals are among the most expensive in the world and finding a room from Denmark is very hard. From second year most students share a house or flat, which is where the real cost appears.
healthcare: Health cover depends on the province, and the difference is large enough that it belongs in the jurisdiction rows on this page rather than in a sentence. Ontario leaves international students outside the public plan altogether and enrols them in UHIP instead, which is a cost for the whole degree. British Columbia, Alberta and Nova Scotia all admit international students to their provincial plans, each on its own condition and each after a wait during which you need private insurance. Quebec requires continuous health and hospitalisation cover for the entire study stay as a condition of the CAQ. The EHIC and the Danish yellow card are not valid anywhere in Canada.

institutions.name: University of Toronto
institutions.englishBachelors: Three campuses and hundreds of programmes; in Arts & Science you are admitted to a broad stream and choose your subject at the end of first year.
institutions.note: Canada's largest and most research-heavy university, with the highest international tuition in the country and famously demanding first-year grading; apply through OUAC.

institutions.name: University of British Columbia
institutions.englishBachelors: Broad degrees in Arts, Science, Commerce, Engineering and more, across Vancouver and Okanagan campuses.
institutions.note: Publishes its international tuition openly and caps annual increases at 3% for four years after you start, which makes budgeting a four-year degree genuinely possible; apply through EducationPlannerBC.

institutions.name: McGill University
institutions.englishBachelors: English-language teaching in a French-speaking city; admission is unusually transparent and almost purely grade-based.
institutions.note: The most Europe-like of the big Canadian universities: it publishes minimum IB scores by faculty, does not ask for essays for most programmes, and Montreal is the cheapest large city on this list to live in.

institutions.name: University of Waterloo
institutions.englishBachelors: Best known for co-op degrees that alternate study terms with paid four-month work terms, typically six of them across the degree.
institutions.note: If you want to graduate with two years of paid professional experience and a network of employers, this is the place - but computer science and software engineering admission is brutally competitive and requires a supplementary application.

institutions.name: Queen's University at Kingston
institutions.englishBachelors: A compact residential campus in a small city - the closest thing Canada has to an American liberal arts experience inside a research university.
institutions.note: Strong community feel and a very high first-year residence rate; the Commerce programme is one of the hardest undergraduate admissions in Canada.

institutions.name: McMaster University
institutions.englishBachelors: Known for problem-based learning, which it pioneered in medicine and now uses across health and science programmes.
institutions.note: The Bachelor of Health Sciences is one of the most sought-after undergraduate programmes in Canada and uses a supplementary application; the rest of the university is more accessible.
institutions.ibPageNote: Checked 2026-09-23. McMaster publishes no IB page. The URL previously recorded here — future.mcmaster.ca/admission/requirements/ — now redirects to future.mcmaster.ca/apply/requirements/, which is a form: you pick a programme and tick "International Baccalaureate" and it generates the requirement. There is no URL that shows the IB requirements on their own.

institutions.name: Western University
institutions.englishBachelors: Large first-year cohorts in broad faculties, with entry into Ivey Business School and other professional schools after year two.
institutions.note: Handles Provincial Attestation Letters transparently and publishes guidance for international applicants; Ivey's two-year HBA is entered after first or second year, not directly from school.

institutions.name: University of Alberta
institutions.englishBachelors: A large research university with strong sciences and one of Canada's biggest engineering faculties.
institutions.note: Consistently cheaper than Toronto or Vancouver both in tuition and rent, with world-class machine learning research; Edmonton winters are genuinely severe.

institutions.name: University of Calgary
institutions.englishBachelors: Professional and applied programmes with strong co-op options, an hour from the Rocky Mountains.
institutions.note: A younger, more applied university with good graduate employment in energy and technology; the outdoor access is the best on this list.

institutions.name: Simon Fraser University
institutions.englishBachelors: Trimester system with three equal terms a year, so you can start in September, January or May and finish faster.
institutions.note: The three-term calendar and large co-op programme make SFU flexible if you want a mid-year start or a shorter overall degree; less prestigious than UBC but noticeably easier to enter.

institutions.name: University of Victoria
institutions.englishBachelors: Mid-sized, heavily co-op, on Vancouver Island with the mildest climate in Canada.
institutions.note: A good choice if a large city is not the point: smaller classes than UBC, strong environmental and ocean science, and a campus you can walk across in ten minutes.

institutions.name: Dalhousie University
institutions.englishBachelors: The main research university of Atlantic Canada, in a small maritime city with a large student population.
institutions.note: Halifax is affordable by Canadian standards and feels a bit like a Nordic port city; Dalhousie's ocean science is genuinely world-class.

institutions.name: University of Ottawa
institutions.englishBachelors: Fully bilingual: you can take a degree in English, in French, or mix the two within the same programme.
institutions.note: In the capital, across the street from Parliament, with internships in government and international organisations; the bilingual option is unusual and genuinely useful.
institutions.ibPageNote: Checked 2026-09-23. The URL previously recorded here — /study/undergraduate-studies/international-applicants/other-recognized-country-curriculum — now redirects to the general programme-prerequisites page, which says nothing about the IB. uOttawa's IB line has moved to /study/undergraduate-studies/program-prerequisites/admission-requirements-international-applicants, which answers 403 to every automated request and "Access denied" to a browser driven from here, so it could not be read and is not recorded. The block is by path rather than site-wide — uOttawa's other links here fetch normally — so the host is not in the link policy.

institutions.name: Concordia University
institutions.englishBachelors: English-language, urban and applied, with strong creative and business programmes and a co-op option.
institutions.note: Less selective than McGill and cheaper than most of Ontario, with the same Montreal advantages; apply directly, not through a central system, and note that Quebec has its own study permit financial rules.
